full_judgment: 10. The presumption shall, however, not come into play if the contrary is proved. In case the registered letter is delivered to the addressee of any person authorized by him or its receipt is refused, there is no difficulty to say that the presumption holds good. But where the letter does not get served in the normal course and is returned to the sender with endorsement such as, "Left", "Not found", "Not claimed" and so on, it will be for the court to decide what is the import of the endorsement on the returned cover of the registered letter having regard to the circumstances in the case. The question being one of fact has to be considered on its own particulars.
